Contributing Researcher: Dr. William Clarke

This has been a truly remarkable stop. My colleagues determined early on that this planet would be suitable for habitation. I've dedicated the majority of my time here to assessing the nearby landscape to determine the best place for future settlements.

Based on the topography of the nearby landscape, some terraforming will be required if the Empire decides to establish a settlement here. However, my analysis of the bedrock suggests that it will play nice with demolition equipment. Construction teams should have no significant issues leveling large sections of terrain for building.

items.source_en:
Dock Seventeen sat above a rust-colored moon, bolted onto an aging trade ring that should have been decommissioned years ago. Power flickered in predictable cycles, and the air smelled faintly of coolant and burned caf. Freighters from a dozen minor syndicates rotated through the bay, their crews keeping their heads down and their transponders quiet. Out here, paperwork mattered less than reputation.

A courier slipped in under an outdated clearance code, carrying a sealed case stamped with an obsolete corporate mark. The delivery was late, the recipient missing, and the station’s local broker was already asking careful questions. By the time security realized something was wrong, the courier had vanished into the lower decks, and several captains were reconsidering how badly they needed their next payout.

[This holobook chronicles a tense stopover on a forgotten trade station, where criminal interests, failing infrastructure, and one misrouted package collide, forcing ordinary spacers to choose between staying invisible or getting involved.]

도킹 17번 구역은 녹슨 빛깔의 달 위에 자리 잡고 있었으며, 수년 전에 퇴역했어야 할 낡은 무역 고리에 볼트로 고정되어 있었다. 전력은 주기적으로 깜빡였고, 공기 중에는 냉각제와 탄 커피 냄새가 희미하게 났다. 십여 개의 소규모 신디케이트 화물선들이 이 구역을 드나들었고, 승무원들은 고개를 숙인 채 송신기를 끄고 다녔다. 이곳에서는 서류 작업보다 평판이 더 중요했다.

한 연락책이 구식 통관 코드를 이용해 잠입했고, 유효기간이 지난 기업 마크가 찍힌 밀봉된 상자를 운반하고 있었다. 배달은 늦었고 수령인은 사라졌으며, 정거장의 현지 중개인은 이미 의심스러운 질문을 던지고 있었다. 보안팀이 무언가 잘못되었다는 것을 깨달았을 때, 연락책은 이미 하층 갑판으로 사라진 뒤였고, 몇몇 선장들은 다음 보상을 받기 위해 얼마나 더 위험을 감수해야 할지 고민하고 있었다.

[이 홀로북은 잊힌 무역 정거장에서 벌어진 긴장감 넘치는 정박 사건을 기록하고 있다. 범죄 조직의 이해관계, 무너져가는 기반 시설, 그리고 잘못 배달된 소포 하나가 충돌하면서 평범한 우주 여행자들은 투명 인간으로 남을지, 아니면 사건에 휘말릴지 선택해야 하는 상황에 놓인다.]

[My Life, Chunk by Chunk] 

I was very young, only seven years old, when I realized - humans are animals. Smart animals, sure, but still animals. You give us food, we'll eat it. We want it to taste good, and we want it to stop our hunger - those two things, that's what's most important. After that, sure, some people want their food to be really 'healthy,' as the experts say. And some want it to be pretty. But most people, they just want to cram something into their face. And that's when the concept of Chunks was born. 

[So begins the 120-page autobiography of Fred Blombart, founder of the Chunks food franchise.]

items.source_en: Under the guise of resistance, they justified violence against the very systems working to rebuild and protect the galaxy. items.source_en:
[An excerpt from Layne Vren’s holobook, Iron Tides, a speculative history chronicling the forgotten struggles of Outer Rim salvage crews as they navigate the dangers of corporate warzones.]

...Rheza just sighed. The drone's photoreceptors flickered, its chassis twitching slightly as its gyros recalibrated, unsure whether to flee or fight. But machine-relations were Rheza's specialty. She toggled the settings on her wrist-link, letting the encoded pulses translate her intent.

"It's alright," she signaled through the interface. "Not here to scrap you. But if we want any chance of getting off this wreck, we’ll need to cooperate."

She hadn't expected her day to go like this—pinned under the remains of a fallen bulkhead on an abandoned ore hauler while trying to bargain with a jittery repurposed security drone. But years of dealing with black-market salvage ops had trained her for worse.

The drone let out a short, modulated chirp. "Compliance… uncertain." It wasn’t an exact translation—battle-droid linguistics always had gaps when shifted into organic speech patterns. But it was close enough. Its posture changed, tension in its servos relaxing slightly. Its primary lens adjusted, focusing on her, scanning, assessing. And then, slowly, it extended a rusted manipulator.

"That’s the way," she signaled back, gripping the appendage and pulling as firmly as she dared. The bulkhead shifted, and with a final heave, the drone was free.

"Better, right?" She tapped out another command. "Now, if you can find a path through this wreck, I’ve got a way off-ship. And maybe—if you’re willing—I can get a signal back to your people. Let them know they’re not forgotten."

A pause. Then, a flicker of blue light from its core. Understanding. The drone adjusted its joints and rolled ahead, its battered frame casting long shadows against the shattered corridor walls. Every few meters, it would pause, ensuring she could keep up…
items.legacy_ko:
[아우터 림의 청소부 요원들이 기업 전란의 위협 속에서 사투를 벌였던 잊힌 생존의 흔적을 기록한 역사 공포서, 레인 브렌의 홀로북 '강철의 조수'에서 발췌한 대목입니다.]

...레자는 그저 깊은 한숨을 내쉬었다. 자이로 장치를 재조정하느라 도망쳐야 할지 맞서 싸워야 할지 갈피를 잡지 못하는 드론의 광학 렌즈가 연신 파르르 떨리며 본체마저 기이하게 덜덜거렸다. 하지만 이 같은 폭주 기계들과 교감하여 길들이는 것은 평생 레자의 독보적인 전문 분야였다. 그녀는 손목에 찬 인터페이스 링크 장치 단추를 조심스레 눌렀고, 암호화된 주파수를 발신해 자신의 온전한 의도를 드론에게 전달했다.

“괜찮아, 해치지 않아.” 그녀가 기계 제어 창을 통해 신호를 보냈다. “널 고철로 분해하러 온 게 아니야. 하지만 이 다 부서져 가는 조난선에서 우리 둘 다 무사히 탈출할 기회를 쥐고 싶다면, 우린 어떻게든 서로 협력해야만 해.”

그녀 역시 오늘 하루의 일과가 이렇게 흘러가리라곤 전혀 상상조차 하지 못했다. 버려진 어느 광물 수송선의 무너진 철골 아래 깔린 채, 공포에 사로잡혀 폭주하기 직전인 보안 드론을 타이르며 은밀한 거래를 벌여야 하는 기괴한 상황 말이다. 하지만 아우터 림의 악랄한 암시장 일대를 구르며 뼈저리게 터득해 온 임기응변 요령 덕분에, 레자는 이보다 훨씬 더 참혹한 지옥에서도 버텨낼 준비가 되어 있었다.

드론이 전자 주파수 소리를 내며 나지막한 기계음을 뱉었다. “수용... 불확실.” 인간의 자연스러운 감정과 어휘로 치환하기에는 군용 배틀 드론의 언어 체계에 태생적인 괴리가 있을 수밖에 없었다. 하지만 의도는 제법 확실하게 전달되었다. 기체는 이내 공격적인 자세를 늦추며 구동 모터의 팽팽한 긴장을 가라앉혔다. 녀석의 중심 광학 렌즈가 초점을 조율하더니 레자를 꼼꼼히 스캔하며 신원을 정밀하게 확인하기 시작했다. 이윽고 녀석은 녹슨 기계식 금속 팔을 천천히 앞으로 뻗었다.

“그렇지, 착하다.” 그녀가 기쁘게 신호를 보내며, 녀석의 튼튼한 금속 손을 꽉 그러쥐고는 힘껏 뒤로 잡아끌었다. 쇳덩이 잔해가 둔탁하게 덜컹거리며 마침내 들어 올려졌고, 마지막 발악과 같은 힘과 함께 드론은 마침내 그 무거운 철골에서 몸을 빼내는 데 성공했다.

locations.vanilla_source_en:
[An excerpt from Lubov Song's novel, "Red Rover, Come Over," an alternate history where autonomous robotic rovers gained sentience, replicated, and colonized Mars before humans could form colonies.]

...Larysa just smiled. The machine continued to blink its lights and emit faint whines as its servos whirled, unsure of how to proceed. But machine-communication was Larysa's specialty. She flicked the buttons on her universal comm unit, its LEDs blinked rapidly in response to her movements.

"It's okay," she signaled through the device. "I won't hurt you. But, if we've any hope of getting out of this cave, we'll need to work together."

Larysa hadn't expected her day to go like this, trapped in a disused mining tunnel under the surface of Mars with a frightened and potentially hostile maintenance robot, but her espionage training had prepared her for similar situations. 

The machine clicked and beeped in response, "I trust you." It wasn't a direct translation. As precise as machine binary language was, there was still a lot of room for misinterpretation when translated to her native tongue. It was close enough. The robot seemed to relax. Its glowing aperture expanded to let more light in as it gazed at her, taking in any information it could gleam from her. And then, it extended one of its many clamps in her direction. She took hold and with a firm, yet gentle tug, pulled the small robot out from under the rubble.

"There we go. That's better, isn't it?" She asked, clicking out her message on her comm unit. "Now, if you can lead me out of this tunnel and back to my drop ship, I can call for backup that could help your fellow machines fight back against your oppressors."

The robot seemed to nod in understanding. and began to wheel its way down the rocky corridor, stopping every so often to let Larysa catch up...
